newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark's Berendsen to split into two listed firms.
newsitem.headline: Denmark's Berendsen to split into two listed firms.

text.p: Denmark's Sophus Berendsen said on Thursday that it planned to split into two separately listed companies.

A statement from Berendsen, which owns 35.8 percent of Britain's Rentokil Initial, said that it would propose at an extraordinary general meeting later this year that the present Sophus Berendsen A/S holding group be divided into Sophus Berendsen A/S and Ratin A/S.
Existing shares would be cancelled and replaced with stock in the new companies, it said.
It said that the new Berendsen company would own all the full subsidiaries in the Textile Service, Power and Motion Control and Electronics and Data sectors and about 3.6 percent of Rentokil Initial.

Ratin would own the remaining 32.2 percent of Rentokil Initial stock, the statement said, adding that the aim of the reorganisation was to end the large holding discount on Berendsen's Rentokil Initial stake and to make valuation of the various group activities easier.
It said the plan was to make the split effective from January 1, 1997, for accounting purposes. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
